tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. ## 0. How the material defines "class" and "twin" (and the other corpus rules)

Mat. §0 (rules of jalon 3), quoted in substance:

- **Rule 1, oracle.** "Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer »." For the reference, the sources MM-02 v0.4 / MM-03.3 v0.3 are superseded by spec v0; expected verdicts must be re-derived from spec v0 clauses (column "spec v0" below), and every change against the material verdict is reported, not applied silently (rule 4).
- **Rule 2, twin.** "**Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction." For MM2-H the table has an explicit column "Jumeau `ok`" (twin of a `ub`). The material itself pairs H37 (ok) with H21b (reject) as "jumeau négatif".
- **Rule 3, reached states.** "Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés."
- **Rule 4.** "Pas de correction silencieuse. Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause."
- **Rule 5, class.** "**Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3." MM2-H and MM23-H tables have no class column (MM2-H is N2 by construction; MM23-H is R; J3 assigned H14 → spec 3, H17 → spec 4/11). W1–W3 are not classed by the material (J3 (f) 17 chose Lib).
- **Rule 6, coverage** ("Couvert": earlier witness). **Rule 7**: MM2-H "validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence". **Rule 8, known gaps**: a case resting on an unapplied decision (MM23-H15, H16) is "encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu » … jamais présenté comme réussi". The brief now requires H15/H16 to pass.

Draft pattern satisfying rules 2–3 (reusable, see §5): `run` from `PS.init statics` with a frame-less fallback `stuckPS` (H3:27, H3:37), `run_reach` (H3:48), `run_ok_of_reach` (H3:54); `sst`/`sstuck`, `sim_of`, `sst_ok_of_reachable` (H23:264, H23:273, H23:301, H23:353); `drun`/`final`/`final_reach` (DS:268, DS:887, DS:890). Verdicts are stated with the operation's relation (`TransferStep … .reject`, etc.) on the reached state.

## 1. Clause table

Status legend. **SAME**: the draft case states the verdict spec v0 gives, on a construction admissible in spec v0 (it still has to be replayed on the reference machine). **DIFFERS**: the draft verdict, construction or a lemma it uses diverges from spec v0 (detail given). **MISSING**: no draft encoding. Each item: clause, change, proof impact on existing draft theorems.

1. **Library state separate from `S₃`, one registry of live administrations** (§38, §46, §47, §55, §56, §75). Library state = arenas, pools, stacks (+ fresh pool/mark ids, resolution ghost) beside the kernel state; library `Reachable` = kernel steps + library ops, each library op proven to be a sequence of kernel steps. Impact: `S3.arenas` and `Reachable.newArena/issue/reset` (M3:250, M3:8369–8373) disappear, so every corpus run (`run` H3:37, `sst` H23:273, `drun` DS:268, `prun` HP:1654) and every `PReach`/`Reachable` statement must be re-based; `h31.pools = [plA]` (H3:590), `w1.pools = [plW]` (H3:827) keep their meaning; `case_stacks` DS:962 conjunct 3 (`kexec … .newArena 1 8`) has no counterpart.
2. **`MetaRight` = `Modify` exercisable on the administering value** for arenas, pools, stacks (§36, §77.1, §78.1). Drop `via`. Impact: `H21` H3:400 run fails at `issue` (verdict flips; add the twin with a `Modify` param); `pool_freeSlot_shared_right` H3:939 flips; `ce_writeShared` DA:1283 conjuncts 4–5 flip; all other cases unchanged (Modify branch used).

## 4. Spec problems (with passage and example)

**P1. `HandlePool` and `DataStack` contracts are outside `specs/`, yet the brief requires their verdicts.** §75: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here." AGENTS.md: "`specs/` is normative and the only source of semantics." Spec v0 constrains them only through §36 (`MetaRight`), §56 (guard), §37 and §89 ("a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure"), §9. Examples with no deciding clause: H31b (`resolveMany Modify` with two handles on one entry → `fail` or `reject`?); `pool_free_entry_handle` H3:977 (`freeSlot` of a free slot at its current generation: v0.4 D.3 only says it "n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité"); `case_aba` DS:927 (`rewind` of a removed mark → `fail`); `freeSlot` with a derived `internal` (v0.4 D.3 vs §69.2 literal). These verdicts cannot be fixed from the spec.

**P2. MM23-H15/H16 expected verdicts rest on jalon-2 decisions 2 and 3, which spec v0 does not contain.** §82.3: "an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"; §81 leaves "representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); … encodings (Spec 11)" undetermined. Example: run R6 (H23:745) `issue [5, 4]` into 2, leaf 4 at offset 0, leaf 5 at offset 8: writing address base+8 (head) or base (lowest) both satisfy §82 as written. The brief says H15/H16 "must now pass"; that requires a recorded decision (spec text or DESIGN.md parameter of the refinement relation), not a silent choice.

**P3. MM23-H09: deallocation of automatic storage at `exitFrame` is not specified.** §9: "The kernel also represents storage with static or automatic duration, whose particular rules will be defined later." §73: "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places." Example: R1 exit (H23:503) — a realization emitting three `DeallocStep` for locals 0, 1, 2 and one emitting none both satisfy §73 and §82.5; the material expects three.

**P4. Byte-copy provenance (MM2-H13a, MM23-H04/H13).** §10: "Rules for propagation of provenance during byte copies and reinterpretations are not yet fixed"; §19: "Undecided: … propagation through representation copies." Against §20.2 (a read "supplies the sequence of abstract bytes actually read, including provenance") and §16 (a write stores "the supplied representation and its provenance information"). Example: `ReadStep` of an 8-byte pointer returns `[init v (some a)]×8`; a `WriteStep` supplying those abstract bytes stores `some a` by §16, but §10 says the copy's propagation is not fixed. H13a "la provenance de chaque octet est conservée" holds at relation level only if the copy supplies the read abstract bytes; at language level it is open.

**P5. `transfer` creating an ownership cycle not caught by any listed precondition.** §63 lists no arrival-usability clause; §63.8 checks only `corr(r)`; §58: "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants." Example: x (Init) owns y (alloc owner x), y owns z (alloc owner y, leaf, Uninit); `transfer(x, z)`: §63.1–§63.5 hold; §63.6–§63.7 are vacuous for the then-unusable places; §63.8 holds (root of y covers leaves of y, `corr(x) = z` ∉ footprint(y)); effect: y owned by z, z owned by y — an ownership cycle (§40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable"), active roots of y and z covering unusable places (`NoDangling`, §54). Whether §58 acts as an implicit rejection is not stated. The draft has an explicit clause "`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`" (M3:1243) which spec v0 does not list. Concerns H13's class of cases.

**P6. Frame ownership of `enterFrame` locals is implicit.** §72.2: "introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots"; §39: "Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places"; §70.1 speaks of "an ordinary local directly owned by a frame"; §47 explicitly allows a static owned by another static, with no analogue for locals. Example: H27b's draft shape `(none, some 0, 0)` (H3:505), a local root owned by local 0, is not excluded by any §72 clause; it would be an `OwnedRoot` freeable by §70. The brief treats "locals owned by frame" as a spec v0 rule; the text does not state it.

**P7 (outside corpus scope, for the kernel mapper).** §36: "Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations" vs §71.2: provider "updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata". Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, frame holding only `Observe` on it, `alloc(provider, owner, shape)` passes §71's static preconditions. No corpus case uses it.

**Material ambiguities (not spec defects; keep both readings, rule 4):** H01 reborrow reading (J3 (g) 5; spec v0 §45/§72 accept it); W2 "la vue de colonne" (J3 (g) 6); W3 blocks issued to locals or into the structure (J3 (g) 7); H16 by-value reception (no kernel primitive; §45 defers to Spec 3); W1–W3 class not given.

**Corpus verdicts superseded by spec v0 (rule 1 source change, to be reported, not silent):** H21 ok → reject (§36, §77.1); H50 à arbitrer → reject (§63.8, §77.2); H49, H51 à arbitrer → ok with residual blocking (§65 last ¶, §88); pool witnesses of 1.5.

## 5. Representation choices recommended (change no accepted program)

1. One library-state record beside `S₃` holding all administration registries (arenas, pools, stacks), with one "live `internal` identities" view used by every creation op — §56 requires consulting all registries; how they are stored is free (§56 "Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel").
2. Drop the `via` argument of library ops once `MetaRight` is Modify-only (it no longer selects anything).
3. Keep the draft case pattern: executable run from the initial state, proven sound, with a fallback state that no run reaches (`stuckPS` H3:27, `sstuck` H23:264), verdict stated with the relation, twin in the same theorem.
4. Arena ops as functions on (kernel state, library state) with a theorem "library `ok` ⇒ kernel step sequence" (draft `issue_as_kernel_split` DA:611, `reset_as_kernel` DA:826, `dexec_reach` DS:412 are the models).
5. Uniform `fail` representation for library ops (state unchanged): either `fail` without state (DS:68) or `fail s` with `s` the input (HP:73), not both.
6. One corpus module per corpus (MM2-H, MM3-H + W, MM23-H, new cases), cases named by material ID, docstring = material summary + spec v0 clauses + class + "material verdict / spec v0 verdict" when they differ.
7. Record unencoded cases (section J, H13b, MM23-H14/H17) as docstring-only entries with their destination, no theorem.

Not checked: Lean was not built or run (verdicts "obtained" are those stated by the draft theorems and J3/DER); spec v0 verdicts for H11, H44, W3 under the new `D(dst)` anchor were traced by hand, not executed.

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

## Readings (test construction choices; none changes a verdict of the spec)

1. Context: compatibility = equality of presented authority and token. §17 ¶2 allows other relations; the corpus fixes none.
2. "Access" in H06 is a read; "use" in H10 is a write, so it does not depend on initialization.
3. H08 twins change only the faulty element (alignment 3 → 4; base 100 with alignment 8 → alignment 4).
4. H13a: the pointer is 8 bytes with value bytes `[64,0,…,0]` and provenance 0. Pointer size and encoding are test choices (Spec 11 territory). "Copy byte by byte" = read one source byte, then write one destination byte supplying the `(value, provenance)` just read. That is the only reading under which §16 ¶2 decides the result. Uninitialized bytes cannot be copied this way, because a write always initializes (§16 ¶2); the case does not need it.
5. H13b: provenances 0 and 2 only show that the verdict depends on the undecided conversion rule. Neither is proposed as the rule.
6. H14: "interpreter not callable" = no proof of the static part exists (`¬ (obStat False).stat …`), because `read` takes that proof as an argument.
7. H15: "distinct identities" = distinct keys 0 and 1 of `State.allocs`.
8. Class column: the corpus gives no class column for MM2-H. N2 is the class by construction. For H14, the material's register sends the concurrency content of `stat` to spec 2, but the case itself tests the machine (§20.1 ¶2 b2). H13b has no destination spec in that register, so its class needs arbitration if N2 is not accepted.

## Theorems proved

- `issueKEff_eq` (Part XIV, §77): `issueKEff s E r d = storeEff (splitEff s internal [r]) |A| d`
  (literal).
- `issueRight_iff_split` (§77.5, §61): under `ArenaInv` + static: `IssueRight ↔ SplitPre k s internal
  [r]`.
- `arrival_iff_store` (§77.3, §77.6, §65): under `WF3`, `NoDangling`, `ArenaInv`, static:
  `IssueArrival ↔ StorePre (splitEff …) |A| d` (O8.3 owned-storage half derived via §49.7).
- **`issue_as_kernel`** (Part XIV, §77, §58): `KInv L.kern → (∀ E, arenas[i]? = some E → Live → ArenaInv)
  → ∀ o, IssueC i r d L o ↔ IssueD k i r d L o` — all outcomes, ok states literally equal. No extra
  hypothesis (the v0 text closes the draft gaps: no "not Init", O8.5 in §77.6).
- `resetKEff_eq`: `resetKEff s E = releaseEff (deriveEff s internal (footprint storage) .modify) |A|`
  (literal). `deriveEff_eq_split` (derive and split states equal). `release_after_derive` (I3 → the
  release is always accepted). `resetPre_iff` (WF3, I1, ArenaInv-if-live: `ResetPre ↔ DerivePre ∧
  ResetNoDeps`). `derive_iff_split` (WF3, I1: `DerivePre s src R Modify ↔ SplitPre k s src [R]` for a
  region of existing leaves — "through derive or split").
- **`reset_as_kernel`** (Part XIV, §78, §58): `KInv → ArenaInv-if-live → ∀ o, ResetC i L o ↔ ResetD i L o`;
  the only extra condition on the sequence side is §78.3, kept as an explicit contract check in `ResetD`.
- **`newArena_as_library`** (Part XIV, §56, §57): (1) `NewArenaStep … (.ok L') → L'.kern = L.kern`;
  (2) `LReach → LReachNG`; (3) `∀ Q, (∀ s, Reachable k statics s → Q s) → ∀ L, LReachNG k statics L →
  Q L.kern` (from `LReachNG.reachable`: library runs with or without the guard land in kernel-reachable
  states, issue = split+store, reset = derive+release). Also `newArena_kernel`, `LStepNG.reachable`.
- `newEntry_inv`, `newArena_clause6` (§76.6 redundant under KInv: WF3 ∧ I1 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧
  AnchorOrderHeld ∧ ArenaInv of the new entry).
- ArenaInv preservation (§55): `lInv_newArena` (guard-free base suffices), `lInv_issue`, `lInv_reset`
  (no kernel hypothesis), `lInv_issueC`, `lInv_resetC` (contract ops, under KInv), `lInv_kernel`
  (`KStep k L.kern s' → WF3 L.kern → NoDangling s' → LInv L → LInv ⟨s', L.arenas⟩`), `lInv_stepNG`,
  `lReachNG_inv`, **`lReach_inv`** (`(∀ s, Reachable → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s) → LReach L → ∀ E ∈ arenas,
  Live → ArenaInv`). Supporting: `AKeep` (no authority removed/reactivated, mode/footprint kept, place
  holders kept, active origins kept) with `kstep_akeep` for all 16 ops (incl. exit reanchoring,
  `exit_akeep`), `kstep_fp` (footprints of existing places kept; `footprint_shapeP` for alloc/enter),
  `entryInv_transport`, `entryInv_append`.
- `issue_effect`, `reset_effect` (§77/§78 ok effects: earlier issuances kept, former authorities
  unchanged, only `I dst` / no `I` change, D only at dst / unchanged, reset record inactive).
- §88: `issue_into_region_rejected` (dst ∈ region → outcome reject, never fail), `issue_keeps_dst`
  (ok → O8.5 holds in the resulting state).
- **`arena_reuse_safe`** (§78, §86): after `ResetD i L (.ok L₁)` and any run `LRun k L₁ L₂`, every `j` with
  `internal ∈ ancs j` covering a storage leaf in `L` is inactive and exercisable at no mode in `L₂`
  (no access possible). `arena_reuse_safe_issued`: same for every issued block with a nonempty region
  (given `EntryInv`). `reset_ends_covering`, `lstep_akeep`, `LRun.akeep`.
- §56: **`live_internal_unique`** (`LReach → Unique56`: two live entries at distinct indices have
  distinct `internal`), via `unique56_step` (guard, no reactivation, issue/reset keep `internal`).

## Counterexamples (spec problems), proven by decide on library-reachable states

Runs from `LState.init Examples.st` under `Examples.K0`: `derive(1,[1],M)`, `store(3,0)`,
`newArena(1,3)` (`Witness.w3_reach`).

1. **§78.3 remark false** — `Witness.reset_clause3_not_implied`. After `issue(0, [], 2)` (= `split(3,[[]])`,
   `store(4,2)`), state `c4`: `LReach K0 st c4`, `KInv ∧ KAux` (via `KInvB`), the entry is live,
   `MetaRight`, §78.2 holds, `I3` holds, but `¬ ResetNoDeps` (usable place 2 has anchor 4, active, empty
   footprint, `3 ∈ ancs 4`); `ResetC 0 c4 .reject` while `derive(3, [1], M)` and `release` are `ok`.
   Quote: "Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active
   descendants covering the storage". Consequence: §78.3 is an explicit check (`ResetD.contract`);
   the §78 effect sentence "an empty-footprint derivative may remain active" holds only for
   derivatives anchoring no usable place.
2. **§86 last sentence contradicted** — `Witness.reissue_reads_former_value`. `issue(0,[1],2)` (block 4),
   `write(4,[1])`, `endUse(2)`, `reset(0)` (derive 5, release 5), `issue(0,[1],2)` (block 6): final state
   `r8` is library-reachable, `KInv ∧ KAux`, `I 1` was `Uninit` before the first write, `Init` after it,
   still `Init` after reset and reissue; block 4 inactive; block 6 active on `[1]` held by 2; and
   `Read3Step 6 [1] r8.kern (.ok _)`. Quote §86: "Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical
   value without the required initialization." The detailed rules (O9.1 asks only `Init`; §78 "No leaf
   is made `Init` by `reset`" and no rule makes it `Uninit`; §77 initializes only the destination) permit
   it. Arbitrate: confirm that the sentence only restates O9 (reading R2 of the mapping), or add a reset
   effect ending the values of the storage leaves (no longer derived from O1–O16 per Part XIV).

## Readings taken (not fixed by policy; each changes no accepted program unless stated)

- §46 sets as lists read by membership; entries identified by index, never removed, liveness derived.
- §55 "still-issued" = block authority active (draft reading; P3). The membership reading is
  stronger; both are invariants, the choice changes only the strength of `ArenaInv` as a hypothesis.
- §55 item 4 "two still-active issuances": `e ≠ e'` over `issued` (set reading).
- §55 item 5 "derivative of internal" = `internal ∈ ancs e.2`; "complying with exclusivity and validity
  rules" left to `Inv3` (§57), not restated. Draft conjunct (direct origin, footprint = region, Modify)
  moved to the auxiliary `IssuedShape`, plus `internal < e.2` (fresh identity), needed to carry §55.5
  through `exitFrame` reanchoring.
- §55 item 6 "anchor and ownership restrictions are respected": no referent, omitted (P4).
- §76.6: not a precondition (no checkable content beyond the invariants; WF3 is not decidable);
  `newArena_clause6` proves it redundant under `KInv`. Draft also omitted it.
- §76 effect: `available := footprint storage` (literal "represents the administered storage").
- §56: registries modeled as lists of live `internal` ids; `others` is a parameter of each `newArena`
  step (library composition supplies it). Uniqueness proven for the arena registry only.
- §77.2 "can legally receive the block value in mode Modify" = `HasRight s .modify dst` (draft).
- §77.3 static part: no list given, omitted (P6). O8.3's owned-storage clause is not restated;
  `arrival_iff_store` shows it follows from §77.2 + §49.7 + NoDangling, so no outcome changes.
- §78.1 "internal and the arena's other restrictions remain valid" and §78.3 "Validity obligations of
  other nested arenas remain satisfied": no checkable condition beyond `ArenaInv`, omitted (P5).
- §78.3 "depends, directly or transitively": an anchor `x ∈ D q` of a usable place `q` with `internal ∈
  ancs x`; contained values are covered because their places are usable places (all checked).
- Reset kernel effect: per Part XIV the sequence consumes identity `|A|` and leaves an inactive record
  (`resetKEff`); the contract kernel effect is defined so (§78 states only metadata and "no Init").
- `ResetD` does not check `MetaRight`/liveness itself (they are `derive`'s §60.1, `resetPre_iff`);
  `IssueD` keeps the issue static checks as the task prescribes.
- `LStep.kernel` admits any `KStep` (non-administrative code is unrestricted).

## Not proved / open

- `lInv_kernel` takes `NoDangling` of the post-state (storage usability of a live arena): it is the
  kernel's §57 guarantee, not proved here. With the transfer defect SP-A1 (kernel-defs report), some
  accepted transfers break `NoDangling`, and `lInv_kernel` is then vacuous for them.
- `issue_as_kernel` / `reset_as_kernel` are stated under `KInv` + `ArenaInv` (live entry) hypotheses;
  `lReach_inv` gives `ArenaInv` from the kernel assembly's `WF3 ∧ NoDangling` on reachable states.
- Draft's stronger reuse statement "every past issuance inactive after reset" (incl. empty regions) is
  not proved: it needs a kernel invariant absent from v0 ("an active derived authority held by a place
  p belongs to D p"). The v0 promise (blocks covering recycled leaves) is proved.
- Not rerun on v0 operations: draft witnesses `ce_two_admins`, `ce_two_admins_ok`, `ce_avail_reject`,
  `ce_g2` as a concrete state, H11/H19/H20/H21/W3 and the §79 scenario.
- Cross-registry uniqueness (§56 for HandlePool/DataStack) — registries outside this scope.

## Differences from the draft (Derived/Arena.lean, MM03 arena section)

Registry moved out of `S3` into `LState`; `issue`/`reset` defined twice (contract and derived) instead
of kernel steps; `IssueStaticR` minus "not Init"; O8.5 added to arrival; `ResetPreR` clauses 2/3 per v0
(covering leaf, strict subtree); `MetaRightM` only; `ArenaInv` per §55 (usability added, conjunct 5
split into §55.5 + auxiliary `IssuedShape`); guard over all registries; `issue_v0_as_kernel` /
`reset_v0_as_kernel` scratch proofs ported; `reset_clause3_strict` and
`reset_blocked_by_stored_internal` dropped (false under v0); `arena_reuse_safe` restated.

153	`release`, §78.3). -/

155	  | .derive src r m => kg L (DerivePre L.kern src r m) (deriveEff L.kern src r m)
156	  | .split src rs => kg L (SplitPre k L.kern src rs) (splitEff L.kern src rs)
157	  | .release a => kg L (ReleasePre L.kern a) (releaseEff L.kern a)
158	  | .transfer src dst => kg L (TransferPre k L.kern src dst) (transferEff L.kern src dst)
159	  | .depend q x => kg L (DependPre L.kern q x) (dependEff L.kern q x)
160	  | .enter ps ls => kg L (EnterPre L.kern ps ls) (enterEff L.kern ps ls)
161	  | .exit => kg L (ExitPre k L.kern) (exitEff L.kern)
162	  | .read a ls => kg L (Read3Pre L.kern a ls) L.kern
163	  | .write a ls => kg L (Write3Pre L.kern a ls) (write3Eff L.kern ls)
164	  | .writeShared a ls => kg L (WriteSharedPre k L.kern a ls) (write3Eff L.kern ls)
165	  | .pin p => kg L (PinPre L.kern p) (pinEff L.kern p true)
166	  | .unpin p => kg L (UnpinPre k L.kern p) (pinEff L.kern p false)
167	  | .endUse p => kg L (EndUsePre k L.kern p) (endUseEff L.kern p)
168	  | .free p auth => kg L (FreePre k L.kern p auth) (freeEff L.kern p)
169	  | .alloc pr ow ls =>

171	      if k.Satisfiable pr ls L.kern then .ok ⟨allocEff L.kern ow ls, L.arenas⟩ else .fail

174	  | .newArena st i =>

187	          else .reject

222	  (lrun k (LState.init statics) os).getD (LState.init statics)

224	/-- A run of `os` from `LState.init statics` (§47) has only `ok` steps and reaches `L`; `L` is
225	library-reachable (Part XIV) and its kernel state is reachable (§57). -/
226	structure RunsTo (statics : Statics) (os : List Op) (L : LState) : Prop where
227	  /-- Every step of the run is `ok` and the run ends in `L`. -/
228	  run : lrun k (LState.init statics) os = some L
229	  /-- `L` is library-reachable (Part XIV, §46). -/
230	  lreach : LReach k statics L
231	  /-- The kernel state of `L` is reachable from `S3.init statics` by O1–O16 (§57). -/
232	  reach : Reachable k statics L.kern
233	
234	/-- The run of `os` from `LState.init statics` has only `ok` steps (§47, §57, Part XIV). -/
235	abbrev Runs (statics : Statics) (os : List Op) : Prop :=
236	  RunsTo k statics os (final k statics os)

238	end Exec

240	/-! ## Soundness -/
241	
242	/-- An `ok` outcome of a relation of `OpRel` is a library step (Part XIV, §57): a kernel step
243	O1–O16 with the registry unchanged, `newArena`, the derived `issue` or the derived `reset`. -/
244	theorem opRel_ok {k : K} {L L' : LState} : ∀ {o : Op}, OpRel k L o (.ok L') → LStep k L L'
245	  | .derive .., h | .split .., h | .release .., h | .transfer .., h | .depend .., h
246	  | .enter .., h | .exit, h | .read .., h | .write .., h | .writeShared .., h | .pin .., h
247	  | .unpin .., h | .endUse .., h | .free .., h | .alloc .., h | .store .., h => by
248	    obtain ⟨h, e⟩ := h
249	    have hL : L' = ⟨L'.kern, L.arenas⟩ := by rw [← e]
250	    rw [hL]
251	    first
252	      | exact .kernel (.derive h) | exact .kernel (.split h) | exact .kernel (.release h)
253	      | exact .kernel (.transfer h) | exact .kernel (.depend h) | exact .kernel (.enter h)
254	      | exact .kernel (.exit h) | exact .kernel (.read h) | exact .kernel (.write h)
255	      | exact .kernel (.writeShared h) | exact .kernel (.pin h) | exact .kernel (.unpin h)
256	      | exact .kernel (.endUse h) | exact .kernel (.free h) | exact .kernel (.alloc h)
257	      | exact .kernel (.store h)
258	  | .newArena .., h => .newArena h
259	  | .issue .., h => .issue h
260	  | .reset .., h => .reset h
261	
262	section Sound
263	variable {k : K} [∀ r r', Decidable (k.DeclaredDisjoint r r')] [DecidablePred k.SharedMutable]
264	  [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.ExternalDone] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
265	  [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] [∀ p ls s, Decidable (k.Satisfiable p ls s)]
266	
267	/-- A guarded kernel step computed by `kg` is an outcome of its relation (§58). -/
268	theorem kg_sound {L : LState} {p : Prop} [Decidable p] {s : S3} :
269	    KRel (Guarded p s) L.arenas (kg L p s) := by
270	  unfold kg
271	  split
272	  · next h => exact ⟨.ok h, rfl⟩
273	  · next h => exact .reject h
274	
275	/-- **Step soundness** (§58, §60–§78): the computed outcome of `o` from `L` is an outcome of the
276	relation of `o`, `ok`, `reject` and `fail` alike. -/
277	theorem lstep_sound (L : LState) (o : Op) : OpRel k L o (lstep k L o) := by
278	  cases o with
279	  | derive => exact kg_sound
280	  | split => exact kg_sound
281	  | release => exact kg_sound
282	  | transfer => exact kg_sound
283	  | depend => exact kg_sound
284	  | enter => exact kg_sound
285	  | exit => exact kg_sound
286	  | read => exact kg_sound
287	  | write => exact kg_sound
288	  | writeShared => exact kg_sound
289	  | pin => exact kg_sound
290	  | unpin => exact kg_sound
291	  | endUse => exact kg_sound
292	  | free => exact kg_sound
293	  | store => exact kg_sound
294	  | alloc pr ow ls =>
295	    show KRel (AllocStep k pr ow ls L.kern) L.arenas _
296	    dsimp only [lstep]
297	    split
298	    · next h =>
299	      split
300	      · next hs => exact ⟨.ok h hs, rfl⟩
301	      · next hs => exact .fail h hs
302	    · next h => exact .reject h
303	  | newArena st i =>
304	    show NewArenaStep [] st i L _
305	    dsimp only [lstep]
306	    split
307	    · next h => exact .ok h
308	    · next h => exact .reject h
309	  | issue i r d =>
310	    show IssueD k i r d L _
311	    dsimp only [lstep]
312	    split
313	    · next hE => exact .noEntry hE
314	    · next E hE =>
315	      split
316	      · next h1 =>
317	        split
318	        · next h2 =>
319	          split
320	          · next h3 =>
321	            split
322	            · next h4 => exact .ok hE h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.ok h4)
323	            · next h4 => exact .store hE h1 h2 (.ok h3) (.reject h4)
324	          · next h3 => exact .split hE h1 h2 (.reject h3)
325	        · next h2 => exact .fail hE h1 h2
326	      · next h1 => exact .static hE h1
327	  | reset i =>
328	    show ResetD i L _
329	    dsimp only [lstep]
330	    split
331	    · next hE => exact .noEntry hE
332	    · next E hE =>
333	      split
334	      · next h1 =>
335	        split
336	        · next h2 =>
337	          split
338	          · next h3 => exact .ok hE (.ok h1) (.ok h2) h3
339	          · next h3 => exact .contract hE (.ok h1) (.ok h2) h3
340	        · next h2 => exact .release hE (.ok h1) (.reject h2)
341	      · next h1 => exact .derive hE (.reject h1)
342	
343	/-- An `ok` computed step is a library step (Part XIV, §58). -/
344	theorem lstep_ok {L L' : LState} {o : Op} (h : lstep k L o = .ok L') : LStep k L L' :=
345	  opRel_ok (h ▸ lstep_sound L o)
346	
347	/-- A run whose steps are all `ok`, from a library-reachable state, ends in a library-reachable
348	state (Part XIV, §46). -/
349	theorem lrun_reach {statics : Statics} :
350	    ∀ {L L' : LState} {os : List Op}, LReach k statics L → lrun k L os = some L' →
351	      LReach k statics L'
352	  | _, _, [], hL, h => by cases h; exact hL
353	  | L, _, o :: os, hL, h => by
354	    unfold lrun at h
355	    cases hs : lstep k L o with
356	    | ok L₁ => rw [hs] at h; exact lrun_reach (.step hL (lstep_ok hs)) h
357	    | reject => rw [hs] at h; cases h
358	    | fail => rw [hs] at h; cases h
359	
360	/-- **Run soundness** (§47, §57, Part XIV): when every step of `os` from `LState.init statics` is
361	`ok`, the run reaches `final k statics os`, which is library-reachable and whose kernel state is
362	reachable by O1–O16. -/
363	theorem runsTo {statics : Statics} {os : List Op}
364	    (h : (lrun k (LState.init statics) os).isSome = true) : Runs k statics os := by
365	  have hr : lrun k (LState.init statics) os = some (final k statics os) := by
366	    unfold final
367	    cases e : lrun k (LState.init statics) os with
368	    | none => rw [e] at h; cases h
369	    | some L => rfl
370	  have hl := lrun_reach .init hr
371	  exact ⟨hr, hl, hl.ng.reachable⟩
372	
373	/-- A computed `reject` is a `reject` outcome of the relation (§58). -/
374	theorem rejects {L : LState} {o : Op} (h : verdictOf (lstep k L o) = .reject) :
375	    OpRel k L o .reject := by
376	  have hs := lstep_sound (k := k) L o
377	  revert hs h
378	  cases lstep k L o with
379	  | ok => intro h; cases h
380	  | reject => intro _ hs; exact hs
381	  | fail => intro h; cases h
382	
383	/-- A computed `fail` is a `fail` outcome of the relation (§58). -/
384	theorem fails {L : LState} {o : Op} (h : verdictOf (lstep k L o) = .fail) :
385	    OpRel k L o .fail := by
386	  have hs := lstep_sound (k := k) L o
387	  revert hs h
388	  cases lstep k L o with
389	  | ok => intro h; cases h
390	  | reject => intro h; cases h
391	  | fail => intro _ hs; exact hs
392	
393	/-- A computed `ok` is the `ok` outcome of the relation to `next k L o` (§58). -/
394	theorem oks {L : LState} {o : Op} (h : verdictOf (lstep k L o) = .ok) :
395	    OpRel k L o (.ok (next k L o)) := by
396	  have hs := lstep_sound (k := k) L o
397	  unfold next
398	  revert hs h
399	  cases lstep k L o with
400	  | ok => intro _ hs; exact hs
401	  | reject => intro h; cases h
402	  | fail => intro h; cases h
403	
404	end Sound
405	
406	end Ern.Corpus
